title: From Non-Coder to Published Dev: How AI Helped Me Release "My Multiverse" on Steam on a Shoestring Budget
author: break200x
selftext:
Hello fellow developers,

I want to share my experience of successfully launching my first game, **"My Multiverse"**, on Steam. As a solo developer with no background in coding or professional game art, I relied heavily on AI-assisted workflows and existing assets to turn my vision into a product, all within a budget of less than $200 USD.

For me, this was less a "game design passion project" and more of a "product management challenge." My goal was to leverage technology to build a full product, handle all backend operations (Steamworks), and bring it to market with minimal financial risk.

**The Workflow:**

* **AI-Assisted Code**: I am not a programmer. I used LLMs (like GPT-4) not to write the code *for* me, but as a co-pilot to teach me the necessary logic and help me debug my C# scripts in Unity.
* **Asset Integration**: I did not create art from scratch. I utilized existing assets and used AI tools (like Midjourney/Stable Diffusion) to generate UI elements, texture variations, and icons to achieve a coherent look for a multi-genre minigame collection.
* **The Build**: The game is centered around a slot machine mechanic that selects random minigames (platforming, driving, arcade-style). The focus was on system integration and game logic using AI-assisted programming.
* **Total Budget**: <$200 USD.

**Why I Am Sharing This:** There is a lot of noise about AI in gaming. My experience is a data point showing how a single person with no technical experience can utilize AI as a "productivity lever" to overcome traditional barriers to entry (code and art creation).

I was not interested in borrowing hundreds of thousands of dollars to build a massive team for a first project. I focused on risk management and asset management to build a marketable product.

I would love to get your thoughts, especially from an engineering or asset management perspective:

1. **System Integration**: Does the transition between AI-assisted systems feel smooth to you as a player?
2. **Product Feel**: Is the integration of various assets and AI-generated elements coherent enough?

Here is the Steam link:[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5080960/My\_Multiverse/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5080960/My_Multiverse/)

comments.body: Im trying to say this in the least harsh was as possible but this is the epitome of AI slop and is what gives AI in game dev a bad rep. There’s a balance to be had imo. Your post was AI, your Steam page is AI, your game is made 100% with AI, your Reddit account is 2 days old and you’re slapping a post here for page views. Folks pour their love into games and spend thousands of hours and this is a little bit of a slap in the face. There’s little artistry here and it feels half assed. Just my 2 cents.
